polity.en: Republic of the Congo (Léopoldville); Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1964
polity.zh: 刚果共和国（利奥波德维尔）；1964年起称刚果民主共和国

summary.en: Henry Morton Stanley founded a station near the Teke villages of Nshasa and Ntamo in 1881 and named it after Leopold II. It replaced Boma as colonial capital (decided 1923, effective 1929) and was renamed Kinshasa by Mobutu in 1966.
summary.zh: 1881年亨利·莫顿·斯坦利在特克人村落恩沙萨和恩塔莫附近建立站点，以利奥波德二世命名。1923年决定（1929年实施）取代博马成为殖民地首府，1966年蒙博托将其改名为金沙萨。

sources.title: Georges Nzongola-Ntalaja, The Congo from Leopold to Kabila (2002)

note: The move of the capital from Boma was decreed in 1923 and completed in 1929; capital status is shown from 1923.

name.zh: 索尔兹伯里堡 / 索尔兹伯里

polity.zh: 罗得西亚和尼亚萨兰联邦
南罗得西亚 / 罗得西亚（1965年单方面独立）

summary.en: The Pioneer Column of Cecil Rhodes’s British South Africa Company raised the flag at Fort Salisbury on 12 September 1890, on land of the Shona chief Neharawa. The city kept its colonial name until 18 April 1982, two years after Zimbabwean independence, when it became Harare.
summary.zh: 1890年9月12日，塞西尔·罗得斯的英国南非公司先锋纵队在绍纳酋长内哈拉瓦的土地上于索尔兹伯里堡升旗。津巴布韦独立两年后，该城于1982年4月18日由殖民旧名改称哈拉雷。

sources.title: UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VII: Africa under Colonial Domination 1880–1935 (ed. A. Adu Boahen, 1985)

summary.en: Named after the 16th-century Portuguese trader Lourenço Marques who explored Delagoa Bay, the settlement grew around a Portuguese fort of 1781. Linked by rail to the Transvaal goldfields, it became capital of Mozambique in 1898 and was renamed Maputo after independence.
summary.zh: 该地以16世纪探索德拉瓜湾的葡萄牙商人洛伦索·马贵斯命名，围绕1781年的葡萄牙要塞发展起来。铁路连通德兰士瓦金矿后，1898年成为莫桑比克首府，独立后改名马普托。

sources.title: Malyn Newitt, A History of Mozambique (1995)

polity.zh: 倭马亚/阿拔斯总督；阿格拉布王朝
法蒂玛王朝与齐里王朝
奥斯曼突尼斯（突尼斯贝伊国）

summary.en: A modest town beside Carthage in antiquity, Tunis rose after the Arab conquest destroyed its neighbour in 698. The Hafsids made it a great Mediterranean capital from 1229, and it has remained the seat of government under the Ottoman beys, the French protectorate and independent Tunisia.
summary.zh: 突尼斯在古代只是迦太基旁的小镇，698年阿拉伯征服摧毁迦太基后兴起。1229年起哈夫斯王朝使之成为地中海大都，此后历经奥斯曼贝伊、法国保护国和独立的突尼斯，一直是政府所在地。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Medina of Tunis
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. III: Africa from the Seventh to the Eleventh Century (ed. M. El Fasi & I. Hrbek, 1988)

polity.zh: 罗马帝国（阿非利加行省首府）
拜占庭帝国（阿非利加总督区）

polity.en: Islamic dynasties of Ifriqiya; Ottoman Tunisia
polity.zh: 伊弗里基叶诸伊斯兰王朝；奥斯曼突尼斯

summary.en: Destroyed by Rome in 146 BCE, Carthage was refounded as a Roman colony under Caesar and Augustus and became the second city of the Latin West. It was the Vandal capital and a Byzantine stronghold until Hassan ibn al-Nuʿman razed it in 698; today it is a suburb of Tunis and a World Heritage site.
summary.zh: 迦太基于公元前146年被罗马摧毁，在凯撒与奥古斯都时期重建为罗马殖民市，成为拉丁西方第二大城。它曾是汪达尔王国都城和拜占庭要塞，698年被哈桑·伊本·努曼夷平；今为突尼斯市郊和世界遗产。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Archaeological Site of Carthage
Procopius, History of the Wars, Books III–IV

note: Wikidata’s end date (146 BCE) refers to Punic Carthage; this genealogy covers the Roman and later city.

polity.en: Caliphal Egypt (Rashidun, Umayyad, Abbasid; Tulunids, Ikhshidids)
polity.zh: 哈里发治下的埃及（正统、倭马亚、阿拔斯；图伦、伊赫什德）

polity.en: Egypt under the Muhammad Ali dynasty (British-occupied from 1882)
polity.zh: 穆罕默德·阿里王朝治下埃及（1882年起英国占领）

summary.en: Founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BCE, Alexandria was the Ptolemaic capital, home of the Library and Pharos, and a centre of Greek, Jewish and Christian thought. After the Arab conquest the capital moved inland to Fustat; the port revived under Muhammad Ali and became a cosmopolitan city.
summary.zh: 亚历山大城由亚历山大大帝于公元前331年建立，是托勒密王朝都城，拥有图书馆与灯塔，也是希腊、犹太和基督教思想的中心。阿拉伯征服后首都内迁至福斯塔特；穆罕默德·阿里时代港口复兴，成为国际化都市。

sources.title: Christopher Haas, Alexandria in Late Antiquity (1997)

polity.en: Caliphal Egypt (Rashidun, Umayyad, Abbasid; Tulunids, Ikhshidids)
polity.zh: 哈里发治下的埃及（正统、倭马亚、阿拔斯；图伦、伊赫什德）

polity.en: Egypt under the Muhammad Ali dynasty
polity.zh: 穆罕默德·阿里王朝治下埃及

summary.en: The Roman fortress of Babylon guarded the Nile crossing; the Arab conquerors built Fustat beside it in 641. The Fatimids founded al-Qahira to the north in 969, and the two merged into the capital of the Ayyubids and Mamluks, the largest city of the medieval Islamic world.
summary.zh: 罗马的巴比伦要塞扼守尼罗河渡口，641年阿拉伯征服者在其旁建福斯塔特。969年法蒂玛王朝在北面建卡希拉，两城逐渐合一，成为阿尤布王朝和马穆鲁克王朝的都城、中世纪伊斯兰世界最大的城市。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Cairo
André Raymond, Cairo: City of History (2000)

note: Fustat was formally abandoned in 1168; it is treated here as the predecessor settlement of Cairo. The Fatimid court moved to Cairo only in 973. Under the Ottomans Cairo was the seat of the province (eyalet) of Egypt.

polity.en: Tuareg seasonal camp, then trading town
polity.zh: 图阿雷格人季节营地，后为商镇
图阿雷格（马格沙伦）统治

polity.en: Pashalik of Timbuktu (Moroccan, later autonomous Arma)
polity.zh: 廷巴克图帕夏国（摩洛哥，后为自治的阿尔马）
图库勒尔帝国与图阿雷格人

summary.en: According to the Tarikh al-Sudan, Timbuktu began around 1100 as a Tuareg camp near the Niger. Under Mali and Songhai it became a hub of trans-Saharan trade and Islamic learning, with the Djinguereber, Sankore and Sidi Yahia mosques and libraries of manuscripts that survive today.
summary.zh: 据《苏丹史》，廷巴克图约于1100年作为尼日尔河附近的图阿雷格营地而兴起。在马里和桑海治下，它成为跨撒哈拉贸易与伊斯兰学术中心，拥有津加雷贝尔、桑科尔、西迪·叶海亚清真寺及至今尚存的手稿图书馆。

sources.title: al-Sa'di, Tarikh al-Sudan (c. 1655), trans. J. O. Hunwick, Timbuktu and the Songhay Empire (2003)

note: Foundation date traditional; the post-1591 sequence of overlords is simplified.

polity.en: Tulama Oromo lands (annexed by Shewa in the 1870s–80s)
polity.zh: 图拉马奥罗莫人土地（1870–80年代并入绍阿）

polity.en: Derg / People’s Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
polity.zh: 德尔格 / 埃塞俄比亚人民民主共和国
埃塞俄比亚联邦民主共和国

summary.en: “New Flower” was founded in 1886 by Empress Taytu and Menelik II beside hot springs at Finfinne, below the older royal seat of Entoto. It became the imperial capital, the seat of the OAU in 1963 and today of the African Union.
summary.zh: “新花”城于1886年由泰图皇后与孟尼利克二世在芬芬温泉旁、旧王都恩托托山下建立。它成为帝国首都，1963年成为非统组织所在地，今为非洲联盟总部所在地。

sources.title: Bahru Zewde, A History of Modern Ethiopia, 1855–1991 (2nd ed., 2001)
Richard Pankhurst, History of Ethiopian Towns from the Mid-Nineteenth Century to 1935 (1985)

note: The start of the Finfinne entry (1800) is an approximation; the Oromo name is older.

polity.en: Kilwa Sultanate (restored, under Portuguese and Omani pressure)
polity.zh: 基尔瓦苏丹国（复国，受葡萄牙与阿曼挤压）
阿曼苏丹国 / 桑给巴尔苏丹国

summary.en: The island city-state of Kilwa dominated the Swahili coast’s gold trade in the 13th–15th centuries; Ibn Battuta called it one of the most beautiful cities in the world. Sacked by the Portuguese in 1505, it declined, and the modern district centre moved to the mainland at Kilwa Kivinje and Kilwa Masoko.
summary.zh: 岛上城邦基尔瓦在13–15世纪主导斯瓦希里海岸的黄金贸易，伊本·白图泰称之为世上最美的城市之一。1505年遭葡萄牙人洗劫后衰落，近代的行政中心迁至大陆上的基尔瓦基文杰和基尔瓦马索科。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Ruins of Songo Mnara
H. Neville Chittick, Kilwa: An Islamic Trading City on the East African Coast (1974)

note: Early dates rest on the Kilwa Chronicle; the 18th-century sequence is simplified.

polity.zh: 阿沃里约鲁巴聚落（贝宁势力范围）
尼日利亚殖民地和保护国

summary.en: Called Eko by its Yoruba and Benin rulers, the lagoon port received its Portuguese name, after Lagos in the Algarve, in the 15th century. A slave-trading kingdom under Benin suzerainty, it was annexed by Britain in 1861 and served as Nigeria’s capital until Abuja replaced it in 1991.
summary.zh: 约鲁巴与贝宁统治者称之为“埃科”，这座潟湖港口在15世纪以葡萄牙阿尔加维的拉各斯得名。它曾是贝宁宗主下的奴隶贸易王国，1861年被英国吞并，并为尼日利亚首都，直至1991年被阿布贾取代。

sources.title: Kristin Mann, Slavery and the Birth of an African City: Lagos, 1760–1900 (2007)

note: The 1472 start follows Wikidata (Portuguese naming); the founding of the Lagos monarchy c. 1600 is approximate.

polity.en: French colony of Chad (French Equatorial Africa from 1910)
polity.zh: 法属乍得殖民地（1910年起属法属赤道非洲）

summary.en: Émile Gentil founded Fort-Lamy on 29 May 1900, naming it after Commandant Lamy, killed five weeks earlier at the Battle of Kousséri against Rabih az-Zubayr. President Tombalbaye renamed the capital in 1973 after the nearby Arab village of Niǧāmīnā.
summary.zh: 1900年5月29日，埃米尔·让蒂尔建立拉密堡，以五周前在与拉比赫·祖拜尔的库塞里之战中阵亡的拉密少校命名。1973年托姆巴巴耶总统以附近阿拉伯村落尼贾米纳之名为首都改名。

sources.title: Mario J. Azevedo & Emmanuel U. Nnadozie, Chad: A Nation in Search of Its Future (1998)

name.zh: 斯坦利瀑布 / 斯坦利维尔

polity.en: Republic of the Congo (Léopoldville); Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1964
polity.zh: 刚果共和国（利奥波德维尔）；1964年起称刚果民主共和国
刚果民主共和国（1971–1997年为扎伊尔）

summary.en: Stanley set up a station below Boyoma (Stanley) Falls in 1883, where the Swahili-Arab trader Tippu Tip was briefly made governor in 1887. Stanleyville was Lumumba’s political stronghold and seat of rival governments in 1960–64, and was renamed Kisangani in 1966.
summary.zh: 1883年斯坦利在博约马（斯坦利）瀑布下设站，1887年斯瓦希里—阿拉伯商人蒂普·蒂普曾短暂任总督。斯坦利维尔是卢蒙巴的政治大本营，1960–64年间为对立政府所在地，1966年改名基桑加尼。

sources.title: Georges Nzongola-Ntalaja, The Congo from Leopold to Kabila (2002)

polity.en: Republic of the Congo (Léopoldville); Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1964
polity.zh: 刚果共和国（利奥波德维尔）；1964年起称刚果民主共和国
刚果民主共和国（1971–1997年为扎伊尔）

summary.en: Founded in 1910 as a copper-mining town and named after Queen Elisabeth of Belgium, Élisabethville was the headquarters of the Union Minière du Haut-Katanga. It was capital of Moïse Tshombe’s secessionist Katanga (1960–63) and was renamed Lubumbashi, after a local river, in 1966.
summary.zh: 伊丽莎白维尔建于1910年，为铜矿城镇，以比利时伊丽莎白王后命名，是上加丹加矿业联合公司总部所在地。1960–63年为冲伯领导的分离主义加丹加首都，1966年以当地河流之名改称卢本巴希。

sources.title: Ludo De Witte, The Assassination of Lumumba (2001)

polity.en: Urban society of the Inland Niger Delta
polity.zh: 尼日尔河内陆三角洲城市社会
杰内城邦（马里势力范围）

polity.en: Moroccan Pashalik, later Bambara Ségou sphere
polity.zh: 摩洛哥帕夏国，后属巴马纳塞古势力范围

summary.en: Excavations at Jenne-jeno, 3 km from the present town, revealed one of the oldest cities of sub-Saharan Africa, occupied from c. 250 BCE. Its successor Djenné became a Niger trading partner of Timbuktu, was taken by Sonni Ali after a long siege, and is famous for its mud-brick Great Mosque.
summary.zh: 距今城3公里的杰内-杰诺遗址发掘出撒哈拉以南最古老的城市之一，约公元前250年起有人居住。继起的杰内成为廷巴克图在尼日尔河上的贸易伙伴，经长期围城后被索尼·阿里攻占，以泥砖大清真寺闻名。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Old Towns of Djenné
Susan Keech McIntosh & Roderick J. McIntosh, “Cities without Citadels”, in The Archaeology of Africa (1993)
al-Sa'di, Tarikh al-Sudan (c. 1655), trans. J. O. Hunwick, Timbuktu and the Songhay Empire (2003)

note: The shift from Jenne-jeno to Djenné (c. 1100–1400) is dated archaeologically; the 1250 boundary is approximate.

polity.zh: 埃塞俄比亚帝国（贡德尔时期）

polity.en: Ethiopian Empire (Zemene Mesafint, “Era of the Princes”)
polity.zh: 埃塞俄比亚帝国（王子纷争时代）

summary.en: Founded by Emperor Fasilides as the first fixed capital of the Solomonic monarchy, Gondar flourished with castles, churches and Ethiopia’s greatest painting tradition. During the Era of the Princes the emperors there became puppets of regional lords, and Tewodros II abandoned it in 1855.
summary.zh: 贡德尔由法西利达斯皇帝建立，是所罗门王朝第一个固定都城，以城堡、教堂和埃塞俄比亚最杰出的绘画传统而繁荣。在王子纷争时代，此地的皇帝沦为地方诸侯的傀儡，1855年特沃德罗斯二世弃之他迁。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Fasil Ghebbi, Gondar Region
Richard Pankhurst, The Ethiopians: A History (1998)

note: Foundation dated 1635 (Wikidata) or 1636; nominal imperial residence until 1855.

summary.en: Capital of the Kingdom of Kongo, renamed São Salvador after its cathedral of the Holy Saviour under King Álvaro I. Sacked and abandoned in the civil wars after 1665, it was reoccupied by Pedro IV in 1709. It took back its Kikongo name after Angolan independence and became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2017.
summary.zh: 刚果王国的都城，阿尔瓦罗一世时以城中救主大教堂之名改称圣萨尔瓦多。1665年后在内战中遭洗劫并被遗弃，1709年佩德罗四世重新入主。安哥拉独立后恢复刚果语旧名，2017年列入联合国教科文组织世界遗产名录。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Mbanza Kongo, Vestiges of the Capital of the former Kingdom of Kongo
John K. Thornton, The Kongolese Saint Anthony (1998)

note: The new name first appears in letters of Álvaro I (r. 1568–1587); 1570 is approximate. The city was largely abandoned c. 1678–1705.

name.en: São Paulo da Assunção de Loanda
name.zh: 圣保罗·达阿松桑·德罗安达

summary.en: Founded by Paulo Dias de Novais in 1576 as the base for Portugal’s conquest of Ndongo, Luanda became one of the largest slave-exporting ports of the Atlantic. The Dutch held it from 1641 until a Brazilian-Portuguese fleet retook it in 1648. It has been the capital of independent Angola since 1975.
summary.zh: 罗安达由保罗·迪亚斯·德诺瓦伊斯于1576年建立，作为葡萄牙征服恩东戈的基地，后成为大西洋最大的奴隶输出港之一。1641年起被荷兰人占据，1648年巴西-葡萄牙舰队将其收复。自1975年起为独立的安哥拉首都。

sources.title: Joseph C. Miller, Way of Death: Merchant Capitalism and the Angolan Slave Trade, 1730–1830 (1988)

polity.zh: 瓦津巴人与早期梅里纳首领
梅里纳王国（马达加斯加王国）

summary.en: According to tradition, King Andrianjaka took the hill of Analamanga around 1610 and garrisoned it with a thousand soldiers, giving it the name Antananarivo, “town of the thousand”. Andrianampoinimerina made it the Merina capital in 1794; the French called it Tananarive.
summary.zh: 据传说，国王安德里亚尼亚卡约在1610年夺取阿纳拉曼加山，派一千名士兵驻守，故名塔那那利佛，意为“千人之城”。1794年安德里亚纳姆波伊尼梅里纳以之为梅里纳都城；法国人称之为“Tananarive”。

sources.title: Pier M. Larson, History and Memory in the Age of Enslavement (2000)

note: The early dates are traditional. The French form Tananarive gave way officially to Antananarivo in the mid-1970s.

summary.en: Captain Alexander Grant founded a British post on Banjul (St Mary’s) Island in 1816 to suppress the slave trade on the Gambia River and named it after Lord Bathurst, Secretary of State for War and the Colonies. Eight years after independence the town took back the island’s Mandinka name.
summary.zh: 1816年，亚历山大·格兰特上尉在班珠尔岛（圣玛丽岛）建立英国据点，以打击冈比亚河上的奴隶贸易，并以陆军和殖民地大臣巴瑟斯特勋爵命名。独立八年后，城市恢复了该岛的曼丁卡语名称。

sources.title: Arnold Hughes and David Perfect, Historical Dictionary of The Gambia (4th ed., 2008)

note: The first entry’s start date is a placeholder for the pre-colonial island under the Kombo kingdom.

polity.zh: 汪达尔人、拜占庭，后为柏柏尔部落

name.zh: 贾扎伊尔·巴尼·马兹甘纳

polity.en: Zirids, Hammadids, Almohads, Zayyanids and others
polity.zh: 齐里、哈马德、穆瓦希德、扎亚尼等王朝
阿尔及尔摄政国（奥斯曼帝国）

summary.en: The Phoenician and Roman port of Icosium was refounded around 950 by the Zirid Buluggin ibn Ziri as al-Jazaʾir, “the islands”, after the islets off its harbour. The brothers Oruç and Hayreddin Barbarossa made it the corsair capital of an Ottoman regency in 1516; France took it in 1830.
summary.zh: 腓尼基与罗马时代的港口伊科西乌姆约在950年由齐里王朝的布卢金·本·齐里重建，以港外小岛得名“贾扎伊尔”（意为“群岛”）。1516年巴巴罗萨兄弟乌鲁奇和海雷丁使之成为奥斯曼摄政国的海盗之都；1830年被法国攻占。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Kasbah of Algiers

note: Roman Icosium declined after the 5th century; the 429–950 entry covers a period with little evidence of urban life.

polity.en: Arab-Berber dynasties, Hafsids, Regency of Algiers
polity.zh: 阿拉伯-柏柏尔诸王朝、哈夫斯王朝、阿尔及尔摄政国

summary.en: Hippo Regius, a royal seat of the Numidian kings, was the see of Augustine from about 395 until his death during the Vandal siege of 430. Under Arab rule it became Būna, the French Bône; since independence it has been called Annaba, the “city of jujube trees”.
summary.zh: 希波雷吉乌斯曾是努米底亚国王的王宫所在，约395年起为奥古斯丁的主教座城，430年他在汪达尔人围城期间去世。阿拉伯统治时称布纳，法国人称博讷；独立后称安纳巴，意为“枣树之城”。

sources.title: Peter Brown, Augustine of Hippo: A Biography (rev. ed., 2000)

note: The Vandals took Hippo in 431 after a 14-month siege. The Arab city grew a short distance from the ancient site.

polity.zh: 罗马共和国，后为罗马帝国

polity.en: Umayyads, Aghlabids, Fatimids, Zirids, Hafsids, Ottoman Tunisia
polity.zh: 倭马亚、阿格拉布、法蒂玛、齐里、哈夫斯王朝及奥斯曼突尼斯

summary.en: A Phoenician foundation older than Carthage, Hadrumetum was renamed after the Vandal king Huneric and then after Justinian before the Arabs called it Susa. The Aghlabids fortified it as the port of Kairouan, building the ribat and Great Mosque that still stand in its UNESCO-listed medina.
summary.zh: 哈德鲁梅图姆是比迦太基更古老的腓尼基城市，先后以汪达尔国王胡内里克和查士丁尼之名改名，阿拉伯人称之为苏萨。阿格拉布王朝把它建成凯鲁万的港口并加固，所建的里巴特和大清真寺至今仍矗立在列入联合国教科文组织名录的老城中。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Medina of Sousse

note: The dates of the Vandal and Byzantine renamings are uncertain; 477 marks the start of Huneric’s reign and 533 the Byzantine reconquest.

polity.zh: 罗马共和国，后为罗马帝国

polity.en: Caliphates, Aghlabids, Fatimids, Zirids, Almohads, Hafsids
polity.zh: 历代哈里发国及阿格拉布、法蒂玛、齐里、穆瓦希德、哈夫斯王朝
奥斯曼的黎波里塔尼亚（1711—1835年卡拉曼利王朝）

summary.en: Oea was one of the “three cities” (tri-polis) of Roman Tripolitania with Sabratha and Leptis Magna, and the region’s name passed to the city after the Arab conquest of 643. Spain, the Knights of St John, the Ottomans and Italy held it in turn before it became the capital of independent Libya.
summary.zh: 欧亚与萨布拉塔、大莱普提斯并称罗马的黎波里塔尼亚“三城”，643年阿拉伯征服后，地区之名转为这座城市的名字。西班牙、圣约翰骑士团、奥斯曼帝国和意大利先后统治这里，后来它成为独立利比亚的首都。

sources.title: John Wright, A History of Libya (2010)

summary.en: Sultan Majid of Zanzibar began a palace town beside the fishing village of Mzizima in 1865–66 and named it Dar es Salaam, “haven of peace”. It became the capital of German East Africa in 1891 and of Tanganyika and Tanzania; the seat of government has moved to Dodoma in stages since 1996.
summary.zh: 1865至1866年，桑给巴尔苏丹马吉德在渔村姆齐齐马旁兴建宫城，命名为达累斯萨拉姆，意为“和平之港”。1891年成为德属东非首府，后为坦噶尼喀和坦桑尼亚首都；自1996年起政府所在地分阶段迁往多多马。

sources.title: James R. Brennan and Andrew Burton (eds.), Dar es Salaam: Histories from an Emerging African Metropolis (2007)

note: Dodoma was designated capital in 1974 and the National Assembly moved there in 1996; ministries followed through the 2010s.

name.zh: 弗雷德里克堡（阿尔戈阿湾）

summary.en: British troops built Fort Frederick on Algoa Bay in 1799. When the 1820 Settlers landed, the acting governor Sir Rufane Donkin named the new town Port Elizabeth after his late wife. In 2021 it was renamed Gqeberha, the Xhosa name of the Baakens River.
summary.zh: 1799年英军在阿尔戈阿湾修建弗雷德里克堡。1820年移民登陆时，代理总督鲁凡·唐金爵士以亡妻之名把新城命名为伊丽莎白港。2021年改名为格贝哈，这是巴肯斯河的科萨语名称。

sources.title: South African Government Gazette: Geographical name changes, 23 February 2021

note: The Cape was under Batavian (Dutch) rule in 1803–1806.

polity.en: Swedish Africa Company (then Danish and Dutch)
polity.zh: 瑞典非洲公司（后为丹麦、荷兰）

summary.en: The Fante town of Oguaa became “Cabo Corso” to Portuguese traders. Swedes built a timber lodge there in 1653, and after England seized it in 1664 Cape Coast Castle was the headquarters of the British slave trade and capital of the Gold Coast until 1877.
summary.zh: 芳蒂人的城镇奥瓜被葡萄牙商人称为“科尔索角”。1653年瑞典人在此建起木结构商站，1664年英国夺取后，海岸角城堡成为英国奴隶贸易的总部和黄金海岸的首府，直至1877年。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Forts and Castles, Volta, Greater Accra, Central and Western Regions

note: The first two entries have approximate start dates.

polity.en: Arab-Berber dynasties; Ottoman beylik of the East
polity.zh: 阿拉伯-柏柏尔诸王朝；奥斯曼东部贝伊辖区

summary.en: Cirta, capital of the Numidian kings Masinissa and Jugurtha, stands on a rock cut off by the gorge of the Rhumel. Destroyed in a civil war in 311, it was rebuilt by Constantine the Great and named after him, a name it has kept in Arabic and French forms. France took it after two sieges in 1836–37.
summary.zh: 锡尔塔曾是努米底亚国王马西尼萨和朱古达的都城，矗立在被鲁梅勒峡谷隔断的岩石上。311年毁于内战，后由君士坦丁大帝重建并以其名命名，此名以阿拉伯语和法语形式沿用至今。法国在1836至1837年两度围城后将其攻占。

sources.title: Claude Lepelley, Les cités de l’Afrique romaine au Bas-Empire (1979–81)

note: The rebuilding and renaming under Constantine is usually dated 313; the 311 boundary marks the destruction.
